issues.description: Inner blocking read loop has no timeout or process-exit backstop, trading a race for a potential deadlock
issues.detail: Once O_NONBLOCK is cleared and the inner while-True read begins, the original safety nets (poll timeout, check_process_exited) are bypassed. A writer that opens the FIFO, writes one byte, then hangs will block the parent indefinitely. The patch substitutes one bug for another. Add a timeout or process-exit check on the blocking path.

issues.description: fcntl mode flip lacks error handling and leaks fd state across the function boundary
issues.detail: F_GETFL/F_SETFL can raise OSError, leaving the fd in an inconsistent blocking state with no cleanup on the exception path. The fd is owned by the caller, so silently clearing O_NONBLOCK violates the frame property. Wrap in try/except and restore flags on exit, or document ownership transfer explicitly.

issues.description: No regression test for the intermittent race the patch claims to fix
issues.detail: An intermittent JSONDecodeError at ~86KB is exactly the failure mode that returns after the next refactor. The fix rests entirely on a prose appeal to POSIX semantics with no fault-injection harness or large-payload test exercising the new blocking path. Add a test that writes a large payload and closes the writer fast.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler reduced to pass, silently dropping has_blocking_error semantics
issues.detail: Previously the handler used content state to detect a closed file and tracked has_blocking_error; now it just continues. Under the new control flow this branch is largely dead code once blocking mode engages, but the behavioral change was bundled silently. Either document the new invariant or split the cleanup into a separate patch.

issues.description: Patch bundles the race fix with deletion of a load-bearing macOS workaround
issues.detail: The removed block existed precisely because POSIX blocking-read behavior was not observed on macOS FIFOs in the past. Asserting POSIX guarantees in the commit message does not justify deleting the workaround without evidence it is now redundant. Either prove the new approach subsumes the macOS path or split the patch.

issues.description: Function contract under writer-crash and writer-hang is unstated and now inconsistent
issues.detail: The old code raised CalledProcessError on empty content; the new code may return a partial buffer on abnormal writer exit, and hang forever on writer stall. Postconditions for failure modes, preconditions on fifo_fd ownership, and the frame on fd state must be written down so callers can rely on the abstraction.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The POSIX blocking-read strategy is the right shape for the diagnosed race, but execution trades an intermittent truncation bug for a potential deadlock: the inner blocking loop has no timeout or process-exit backstop, and fcntl mode changes lack error handling and leak fd state to the caller. The patch also bundles unrelated changes (silent BlockingIOError semantics drop, deletion of a macOS workaround) without justification, and ships no regression test for a race that already reached production. Required: add timeout/process-exit escape on the blocking path, handle fcntl errors and restore fd flags, justify or restore macOS handling, write down the function's contract, and add a large-payload regression test.
